To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
84 of 90 abundant cytoplasmic protein species in HeLa cells pulse-labeled at six time points during the cell cycle were synthesized in approximately the same proportion at all time points.
the synthesis of 90 abundant proteins is relatively constant throughout the HeLa (human cancer) cell cycle.
84 of the 90 most abundant proteins are made in similar proportions at all times during mitotic division.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of proteins during the cell cycle and their possible relationship to the events of cell division.

the synthesis of the proteins that make up the HeLa cell and the changes in the synthesis of the most abundant proteins during the cell cycle, and with the identification of the proteins which vary in abundance during the cell cycle and which may therefore be involved in the regulation of cell division.
the synthesis of proteins in the HeLa cell throughout the cell cycle and the identification of those proteins that vary in their rate of synthesis during cell division.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis of the most abundant proteins is not regulated during the HeLa cell division cycle.
the synthesis of the vast majority of proteins is not cell cycle dependent in HeLa cells.
most of the HeLa cell proteins are made at a relatively constant rate throughout the cell cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there are a large number of proteins which are made throughout the cell cycle at a relatively constant rate and that there is a small but significant number of proteins which vary in frequency of appearance at different times in the cell cycle.
the synthesis of the 90 most abundant proteins in HeLa cells does not vary significantly throughout the cell cycle.

the majority of the abundant proteins are made in a similar proportion of total synthesis at all times in the cell cycle and that the proteins which are made to a different proportion are those which may be involved in cell division.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of HeLa proteins are made in a constant ratio throughout the cell cycle.

there is a remarkable constancy in the proportion of total synthesis of most proteins throughout the HeLa cycle, and the few proteins that vary are those that are likely to be associated with the mitotic apparatus.
the synthesis of most proteins is relatively constant throughout the cell cycle.
